⏱️ 0–2秒 「血与寂静」

⏱️ 4–6秒 「幽灵现身」

⏱️ 6–8秒 「记忆之眼」

⏱️ 8–10秒 「承载重量的语言」

画面镜头类型：过肩交替镜头，电影1.85:1信箱画幅插入

信箱画幅裁切出现——标志对白时刻。越过Shea肩膀拍向CiaO——他在恰好3米处停步。声音低沉、克制、近乎温柔：「もう終わったと思っていた」（我以为一切都已经结束了。）他的下颌几乎纹丝不动。隘道将每个音节放大为教堂混响。切换——越过CiaO肩膀拍向Shea——她的目光从未低垂，从未动摇：「まだよ。終わったことなんて、一度もない」（还没有。从来都没有结束过。）声音平稳，但她受伤的手握得更紧——绷带边缘渗出新鲜血迹。真实。当下。不败。信箱画幅随张力破裂为另一种东西而缓缓扩展回全画幅。

⏱️ 10–12秒 「重量消散」

画面镜头类型：缓慢推进双人镜头，移动轨道加微型升降

摄像机架于移动轨道——缓慢、从容地推向中景双人构图中的两个角色。CiaO的虚空之刃分三个节拍落下——不是丢弃，不是投降——是主动选择放下，暗色能量如余烬消散，每一粒粒子向上漂浮发出微光。Shea的战斗肩膀松开——一口气，两口气——重量从她身体上肉眼可见地离去。黎明之光开始涌入两人之间的空间，隘道本身仿佛在呼气。风格化画意：金色光线轨迹短暂出现在他们脚下之间的地面，如同世界在承认这一刻的存在。配乐涌起——单一大提琴音符渐强生长。

⏱️ 12–14秒 「走向太阳」

稳定器在2米后方跟拍，从地面水平缓缓升起，CiaO与Shea并肩走入隘道深处——他们的脚步自然同步，非刻意为之。@image3的废墟石柱如古老沉默的见证者般夹道而立，尺度将两个人物压缩得渺小而坚定。摄像机随他们行走缓缓上升——从后方低位到后方高位——逐渐揭示前方被不可能的金色黎明沐浴的隘道全貌。他们的影子向后方摄像机方向拉得极长。没有言语

Landing is clean, precise, flawless: both skates contact only ice, never water, with no stumble, slip, knee drop, or loss of balance. Her body absorbs impact smoothly. Video returns to normal speed. The slab bends slightly but holds firm. She glides onto safer frozen ice, performs a controlled sideways braking slide, sprays frost toward camera, stops and looks into lens with fearless expression. prompt:
Use the uploaded image as the exact start frame and the primary visual reference for the lead woman’s face, short black bob haircut, blue eyes, stern expression, and grounded vintage-action-movie realism. Do not turn her into a cartoon, superhero, or glossy CGI character. Create a 14-second live-action sequence, 16:9, 720p or higher, with synchronized audio. Style: late-1990s vintage techno-action thriller, real actors, real set, practical effects, 35mm film grain, slight halation, mild handheld camera shake, hard cuts only, tense pacing, blue-gray lab lighting mixed with flashing red alarm lights. Environment: cluttered computer lab filled with CRT monitors, beige keyboards, server racks, cables, rolling office chairs, flickering screens, smoke haze, sparks, and an emergency exit door at the back.

The woman is with a nervous male computer lab technician, around 30, rumpled office clothes, ID badge, slightly awkward, carrying printouts. Chrome humanoid robots suddenly invade the lab.

TIMELINE

0–3 seconds:

Medium shot. The woman strides into frame beside the lab technician and grabs his arm, annoyed but charismatic. She sharply chides him:

“Don’t you have better things to do than test prompts on the Fourth of July?”

The technician turns, startled. Alarm lights begin flashing.

3–5 seconds:

A chrome humanoid robot smashes through a glass lab door in the background. Another emerges through smoke between server racks. CRT monitors flicker and pop. Quick push-in on the woman as she instantly shifts from irritated to battle-ready.

5–9 seconds:

She pulls a compact futuristic handgun from her belt and fires at the incoming robots. Bright practical muzzle flashes. Loud metallic impacts. Sparks burst from the robots’ chrome bodies. One robot crashes into a monitor cart, another keeps advancing. Handheld camera tracks with urgency but keeps the action readable.

9–11 seconds:

The woman grabs the lab technician with her free hand and yanks him away from the workstation toward the exit while firing one last shot over her shoulder. She shouts:

“Let’s get out of here!”

11–14 seconds:

Tracking shot down the lab aisle as she drags the technician into a run. Robots push through smoke behind them. Overhead cables spit sparks. Papers fly, warning lights flash, boots pound on the floor. End on the woman pulling the technician through the emergency exit as the red alarm light flares across the frame.

STYLE RULES:

Realistic vintage action-film energy. Practical chrome robot suits or animatronic-style enemies, not weightless CGI. Real explosions of sparks, real smoke, real set damage, believable physics, cinematic but gritty. No subtitles, no on-screen text, no logos, no watermark, no comedic slapstick. Technical: 24fps smooth motion, 16:9. No jitter.
Audio: environmental SFX only — wingbeats, forest ambience, one sharp beak snap. No music. No subtitles.

SUBJECT — @butterfly (matches input 100%): amber-orange upper wings with cream border spots, teal-green lower wings, amber-tipped antennae. @parrot (matches input 100%): teal-green body, mustard-gold chest, burnt orange wing flashes, charcoal curved beak, pale-gold eye with cream eye-ring. Emotional beat: playful freedom cut short by a sudden wild strike — startling but storybook, not cruel. WB warm daylight ~5200K. ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE.

LOCATION — a lush sunlit painted forest, STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, not a fixed keyframe. Towering tree trunks in soft teal-green washes, dense canopy with dappled amber light shafts breaking through, drifting luminous pollen. The model freely extends the forest in every direction; the subjects race through deep space — NOT pinned to any input frame.

ACTION — one single unbroken camera move from first frame to last: chase → strike → bullet-time. Absolutely no cuts, no edits, no transitions.
BEAT 1 (0:00–0:04) — camera flies directly behind @butterfly as it flutters fast and erratically through the forest — weaving between trunks, dipping under a low branch, jinking left through a bright shaft of amber light, wings flashing orange and teal. Lively, kinetic, joyful. Brushy motion blur streaks the passing foliage.
BEAT 2 (0:04–0:05) — without any cut, @parrot bursts in from screen-left in a fast diagonal dive and snatches @butterfly out of the air, its charcoal beak biting down and clamping onto the outer edge of one amber wing. The camera sweeps with the strike in the same fluid move.
BEAT 3 (0:05–0:10) — still unbroken, the camera drives in on the moment of capture and time collapses into bullet-time: near-frozen extreme macro of the beak's grip pinching the wing, the wing membrane bending and creasing, shimmering iridescent scale-powder scattering off the pinched edge and hanging suspended motionless in mid-air as tiny painted dabs of light. The camera orbits slowly around the frozen instant — wing veins razor-sharp in painterly detail, @parrot's pale-gold eye and beak texture crisp, @butterfly caught mid-flutter. Hold the orbit to the final frame.

CAMERA — one continuous move throughout. BEAT 1: low chase cam tight behind the butterfly, slightly below its flight line looking up into the canopy light, whipping and banking with every jink — motivation: put the audience on its tail. BEAT 2: the same camera whip-sweeps laterally with the parrot's dive, momentum carried through the strike — motivation: the world intrudes violently into the chase. BEAT 3: the move decelerates into a slow macro orbit around the bite, roughly 120° of arc, ending slightly above and side-on to the parrot's eye — motivation: turn violence into a frozen painted still-life.

STYLE — Dominant: teal/forest-green painted forest depths 60% / Secondary: warm cream-amber sunlight shafts and glowing haze 30% / Accent: the butterfly's burnt-orange wings and the parrot's gold eye 10%. WB ~5200K, sun high behind canopy, backlit haze, dappled light raking across the action.

CONSTRAINTS — 16:9. ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS UNBROKEN SHOT — no cuts, no transitions, no camera teleports. SPEED-RAMP only once: full speed 0:00–0:05, then ramp down into near-frozen bullet-time 0:05–0:10; never ramp back up. Strong painterly motion blur during the chase resolving into crisp frozen detail in the macro. @butterfly stays small real-insect scale, @parrot medium parrot scale — NOT oversized. The beak clamps ONLY the wing edge — no gore, no tearing, wing intact. Characters match reference sheets exactly, no identity drift. NO eye glow. No text, no watermark.

Live-Action + Flat 2D Sticker Composite comedy short video. First-person POV cooking vlog perspective. A strong contrast blend between realistic kitchen cinematography and a flat cartoon sticker aesthetic. 8K ultra HD quality, handheld micro-shake camera movement, vertical screen format.

A chibi anime sticker character (flat 2D sticker texture, cartoon outline, paper-cutout feel): long golden hair with straight bangs, large round purple eyes, pink blush on cheeks, white sailor-style school uniform, and a blue hair clip. The character sits on a small wooden stool beside the stove, about half the height of the wok. The character must remain a purely flat 2D sticker throughout the entire video and must not be converted into realistic 3D style.

First-person overhead POV: a real human hand is stir-frying beef and vegetables with a spatula. The sticker character squints with a mischievous smile, blush becomes stronger, and it raises a glass seasoning jar with both hands.

Taking advantage of the distraction, the character dumps the entire jar of white salt into the wok. A realistic physical waterfall of salt grains pours down, piling up into a small white salt mountain on top of the vegetables.

Sound Effects:
Food sizzling + dense rushing sound of pouring salt.

[00:03–00:05] Shot 2: Spatula Bonk

One real human hand quickly snatches the glass salt jar away from the character. The other hand raises the spatula and gently taps the character on the head with the flat side.

A cartoon-style bonk occurs — a red cartoon bump instantly pops up above the character’s head with a “Duang!” effect. Its entire flat paper-like body bounces up and down from the impact.

Sound Effects:
Metallic spatula “Duang!” hit + cartoon spring bounce sound.

[00:05–00:08] Shot 3: Cry & Feed

The sticker character holds the bump on its head, instantly develops spiral swirl eyes, opens its mouth wide, and starts dramatically crying. Bright blue cartoon tears shoot out sideways like fountains.

The real human hand immediately uses the spatula to scoop a huge amount of salty vegetables covered with white salt from the salt pile. While the character’s mouth is wide open from crying, the hand accurately pushes the spoonful into its mouth, completely stuffing its cheeks.

Sound Effects:
Exaggerated cartoon crying + scraping salt sound + mouth-stuffing “pop” effect.

[00:08–00:10] Shot 4: Salt K.O. Ending

The character’s cheeks puff up into two huge red circles after eating the salty food. It swallows, then its pupils suddenly shrink, its face turns pale, and its whole body freezes and trembles for a moment.

Its eyes transform into two “X” marks. The character falls straight backward from the small wooden stool, lying flat on the counter with its limbs pointing upward. A ring of spinning dizzy stars appears above its head, and a small ghost-like white soul smoke floats out from its mouth.

The frame freezes.

Sound Effects:
Stiff “click” sound + falling “thud” + cartoon ascending spirit sound effect fade-out.

Realistic third person one shot. Ultra-wide 13mm fisheye, natural shake. The surfer is miniature — everything is colossal. The surfer is already riding. The wave face is dirty but glassy, clean peeling line. The board hisses through brown-tinted water. Weight shifts back into the pocket, then drives forward again off the front foot — board accelerates, waterline climbing the rail.

A giant woman crosses the garden behind — bare feet, floral dress, completely unaware. Her foot drops into the puddle with a colossal impact. The shockwave rolls forward, dirty water exploding around her ankle. The puddle surges. A new swell lifts behind the surfer.

The wave steepens and throws. A compact muddy barrel forms — brown-green translucent wall, cracked concrete floor below, the enormous house porch framed in the exit oval. The spit fires dirty foam across the lens. Exit clean onto flat murky water. Grass blades loom at the edge. The woman keeps walking, oblivious.

Camera: ultra-wide fisheye, brown water tint on lens at spit. Real-time, no cuts.

surging, collapsing, reforming, throwing spray and foam as it moves,

water and splinters, the camera pulling into a vast wide as the fleet scatters
